It restricts every gauge to a single-valued Qbar-rational function; records the general endpoint mismatch chi_n(P_n)-chi_0(P_0); states the Hermite--Lindemann beta=1, A=0 exception and that beta=0 has no complex logarithm; keeps log(abs(A_G)) outside scope; places Hénon orbit coordinates in an orbit number field with extended S; preserves repeated-neighbor multiplicity at n=1,2; and makes every stepwise definedness and pole check fail closed. Version 2 SHA-256 was 552ec986fc35d0afb3137050ddf8dfe748647c51b8517293a0e072b9612b1497. No candidate periodic point, action, prime table, zero data, or candidate-derived output was inspected.
positioning: A narrow all-period design certificate for one proposed arithmetic clock, not a new action-spectrum or transcendence theorem.
independence_statement: This candidate tests periodic action rather than the derivative or return-multiplier clocks of earlier projects. It uses no sealed candidate output, external prime table, Riemann-zero data, or target fitting.
research_question: Can the one-traversal periodic action of a frozen algebraically normalized exact potential on an algebraic periodic orbit equal log(p) for any positive rational prime p?

general_setup.phase_space: an algebraic variety X over Qbar with an algebraic symplectic form on the orbit domain
general_setup.map: an algebraic rational map F whose full selected periodic orbit avoids indeterminacies
general_setup.liouville_primitive: a single-valued algebraic rational one-form theta on the orbit domain
general_setup.exact_potential: a single-valued algebraic rational function G satisfying F^*theta-theta=dG wherever evaluated
general_setup.normalization: every additive constant, transition value, endpoint mismatch, or branch contribution that actually enters the action is frozen before orbit evaluation and belongs to Qbar; a uniform autonomous constant gives n*C, while general stepwise gauges give chi_n(P_n)-chi_0(P_0)+sum_j C_j
general_setup.periodic_orbit: P in X(Qbar), P_0=P, P_{j+1}=F_j(P_j) defined step by step, and P_n=P_0; before evaluating each summand, F_j, G_j, theta_j when used, chi_j, chi_{j+1}, and every transition must be defined and pole-free at its required point
general_setup.target: exact equality to the positive real log(p), or to any complex logarithm of a nontrivial algebraic number

primary_claims: C1: Regular evaluation of G on an algebraic period-n orbit gives A_G(P) in Qbar.

C2: If beta is a nonzero algebraic number and exp(A_G(P))=beta, Hermite--Lindemann leaves only the trivial algebraic case A_G(P)=0 and beta=1. Thus no branch of the logarithm of beta in Qbar^* except 1 can equal A_G(P); beta=0 has no complex logarithm. In particular A_G(P) cannot equal log(p) for a rational prime p.
C3: The exclusion survives algebraic scaling, averaging, repetition, real part, imaginary part, modulus, and algebraic additive normalization.

C4: For a single-valued Qbar-rational chi, theta'=theta+dchi and G'=G+chi composed with F-chi+C give A_G'=A_G+n*C on a closed orbit. In general stepwise form the shift is chi_n(P_n)-chi_0(P_0)+sum_j C_j; endpoint compatibility removes only the endpoint term. Algebraic, pole-free endpoint data preserve algebraicity even when they do not match.
C5: Allowing a transcendental additive constant invalidates the broad claim; the identity map with constant potential log(2) is a frozen counterexample.
C6: For H_a(q,p)=(q^2-a-p,q) with algebraic a, G=2*q^3/3-p*q and L_a=q^3/3-a*q-q*Q give opposite-sign algebraic periodic actions at every finite periodic orbit.

C7: Let K0 contain a with a in O_{K0,S0}; for an orbit field K/K0 containing every periodic coordinate, extend S0 to the places S of K above it. Every finite periodic coordinate lies in O_{K,S}, and 3*A_G lies in O_{K,S}.

predeclared_exact_predictions.separately_normalized_step_shift: chi_n(P_n)-chi_0(P_0)+sum_{j=0}^{n-1} C_j; this reduces to sum_j C_j only when endpoint gauges agree under the closed-orbit identification

gauge_ledger.admitted_primitive_change: theta'=theta+dchi only for a single-valued Qbar-rational chi that is regular at every point where chi is evaluated
gauge_ledger.forbidden_target_injection: C=(log(p)-A_G(P))/n or any other orbit- or target-dependent transcendental constant
gauge_ledger.local_or_time_dependent_extension: G'_j=G_j+chi_{j+1} composed with F_j-chi_j+C_j; the exact closed shift is chi_n(P_n)-chi_0(P_0)+sum_j C_j. Compatibility chi_n(P_n)=chi_0(P_0) is an optional simplification, not an unstated assumption.
gauge_ledger.endpoint_mismatch_rule: If Delta_end=chi_n(P_n)-chi_0(P_0) is algebraic and both values are defined, the algebraic source lock survives but the shorter shift=sum_j C_j formula must stop. If either endpoint value is undefined, has a pole, is multivalued without a frozen algebraic transition, or contributes a transcendental value, the absolute-action certificate stops.

stop_rules: If the additive normalization is not frozen and algebraic, report that the broad action claim is false and stop the certificate.

At each j, construct P_{j+1}=F_j(P_j) only after verifying F_j is defined at P_j; before evaluating a term verify G_j(P_j), chi_j(P_j), chi_{j+1}(P_{j+1}), and any transition value are individually defined and pole-free. Any failure stops the corresponding action or telescope claim.
If the orbit is not proved algebraic, do not apply the simple evaluation theorem; do not silently replace this hypothesis by positive-dimensional periodic-locus intuition.
If the primitive change is closed but not proved exact on the orbit domain, stop the gauge-invariance claim and open a separate period ledger; do not apply telescoping.

If a potential, gauge, or chart transition is multivalued or has branch monodromy, stop the absolute-action certificate until every branch transition and monodromy contribution is frozen and proved algebraic.

If local or time-dependent representatives are used, the general shift is chi_n(P_n)-chi_0(P_0)+sum_j C_j. Stop the shorter sum_j C_j formula unless endpoint gauges are compatible. The source lock itself survives an incompatible endpoint only when both endpoint values and every C_j are defined, frozen, and algebraic.
For logarithmic targets, beta=0 has no complex logarithm. For beta=1, retain the trivial algebraic solution A=0; do not claim that all logarithms of 1 are excluded without this exception.
Any apparent exact equality between an algebraic action and log(p) is treated first as a normalization, exact-arithmetic, or target-injection error and triggers an independent proof audit.

For complex action, the certificate may exclude Re(A_G)=log(p), Im(A_G)=log(p), or abs(A_G)=log(p), but it must stop before asserting anything about arg(A_G) or log(abs(A_G)); those are different observables.
Do not infer the all-period theorem from finite low-period calculations; the theorem is the evidence and any later calculation is only an implementation check.
Do not strengthen S-integrality to integrality of A_G itself; absent a separate divisibility proof, stop at 3*A_G being S-integral and track all places above the rational prime 3.
Passing the certificate closes only the normalized algebraic action-as-clock route and must not be reported as excluding all symplectic or arithmetic clocks.
